subject: Cloud Computing
title: Cloud Audit Logging
description: A quick win: understand Cloud Audit Logging.

hook.text: Someone deleted your production database at 2 AM. Without audit logs, you'll never know who or how.

buildup.text: Audit logs record every action: who did what, when, and from where. AWS CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, GCP Audit Logs.

discovery.text: Logs are essential for forensics, compliance reporting, and detecting suspicious behavior patterns.

twist.text: Storing logs costs money. Many companies delete them too soon and lose critical evidence when breaches occur.

climax.text: Best practice: store audit logs in a separate, tamper-proof account. Attackers can't cover tracks they can't reach.

punchline.text: Logs tell the story of what happened. Keep them safe and long.

quiz.question: Why should audit logs be stored in a separate account?
options: So attackers who compromise the main account cannot delete or tamper with logs
Audit logs are too large to store alongside application data
Cloud providers charge extra for logs in the same account

details.summary: Cloud audit logs record every API call and configuration change across cloud accounts, providing a detailed trail for security investigation and compliance. Services like AWS CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, and GCP Cloud Audit Logs capture who did what and when.
details.whyItMatters: Without audit logs, security teams cannot detect breaches, investigate incidents, or prove compliance. Logging is the foundation that all cloud security monitoring and forensics depend on.
takeaways: Audit logs record all API calls and config changes
Enable logging in all accounts and regions from day one
Store logs in tamper-proof, centralized storage

faq.question: What should be logged in the cloud?
faq.answer: All management plane API calls, data access events for sensitive resources, authentication attempts, permission changes, and network flow logs should be captured. Under-logging creates blind spots that attackers exploit during breaches.

faq.question: How long should audit logs be retained?
faq.answer: Retention depends on compliance requirements. Common standards require 1 to 7 years. Many organizations retain 90 days in hot storage for active investigation and archive the rest in cold storage. Logs should be immutable to prevent tampering.
